arxiv-1910-03887.title: Constraint on the Matter-Antimatter Symmetry-Violating Phase in Neutrino Oscillations
arxiv-1910-03887.creator: K. Abe, R. Akutsu, A. Ali, C. Alt, C. Andreopoulos, L. Anthony, M. Antonova, S. Aoki, A. Ariga, Y. Asada, Y. Ashida, E.T. Atkin, Y. Awataguchi, S. Ban, M. Barbi, G.J. Barker, G. Barr, C. Barry, M. Batkiewicz-Kwasniak, A. Beloshapkin, F. Bench, V. Berardi, S. Berkman, L. Berns, S. Bhadra, S. Bienstoc
arxiv-1910-03887.description: Abstract I Introduction The symmetry between matter and antimatter, charge-conjugation parity-reversal ( CP ) symmetry, was believed to be a perfect symmetry of nature. In 1964, asymmetric behavior of particles and anti-particles, CP violation, was observed Christenson:1964fg , and CP violation in the weak interactions of quarks was soon established Tanabashi:2018oca .

arxiv-2112-06726.title: Orbifold Kähler Groups related to Mapping Class groups Thanks: The research of P. E. was partially supported by the ANR project Hodgefun ANR-16-CE40-0011-01.
arxiv-2112-06726.creator: Philippe Eyssidieux, Louis Funar
arxiv-2112-06726.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Philippe Eyssidieux, Louis Funar. We construct certain orbifold compactifications of the moduli stack of pointed stable curves over ℂ \mathbb{C} and study their fundamental groups by means of their quantum representations. This enables to construct interesting Kähler groups and to settle most of the candidates for a counter-example to the Shafarevich conjecture on holomorphic convexity proposed in 1998 by Bogomolov and Katzarkov, using TQFT representations of the mapping class groups.

arxiv-2301-00739.title: On the Complexity of Sub-Tree Scheduling for Wireless Sensor Networks with Partial Coverage
arxiv-2301-00739.creator: Michele Barbato, Nicola Bianchessi
arxiv-2301-00739.description: Abstract Given an undirected graph G G whose edge weights change over s s time slots, the sub-tree scheduling for wireless sensor networks with partial coverage asks to partition the vertices of G G in s s non-empty trees such that the total weight of the trees is minimized.

arxiv-2401-12599.title: Revolutionizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Enhanced PDF Structure Recognition
arxiv-2401-12599.creator: Demiao LIN
arxiv-2401-12599.description: Abstract With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a predominant method in the field of professional knowledge-based question answering. Presently, major foundation model companies have opened up Embedding and Chat API interfaces, and frameworks like LangChain have already integrated the RAG process.

arxiv-2406-01765.title: Reproducibility Study on Adversarial Attacks Against Robust Transformer Trackers
arxiv-2406-01765.creator: Fatemeh Nourilenjan Nokabadi fatemeh.nourilenjan-nokabadi.1@ulaval.ca, Jean-François Lalonde jflalonde@gel.ulaval.ca, Christian Gagné christian.gagne@gel.ulaval.ca
arxiv-2406-01765.description: Abstract New transformer networks have been integrated into object tracking pipelines and have demonstrated strong performance on the latest benchmarks. This paper focuses on understanding how transformer trackers behave under adversarial attacks and how different attacks perform on tracking datasets as their parameters change.

arxiv-2406-06337.title: System- and Sample-agnostic Isotropic 3D Microscopy by Weakly Physics-informed, Domain-shift-resistant Axial Deblurring
arxiv-2406-06337.creator: Jiashu Han, Kunzan Liu, Keith B. Isaacson, Kristina Monakhova, Linda G. Griffith, Sixian You
arxiv-2406-06337.description: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) subcellular imaging is essential for biomedical research, but the diffraction limit of optical microscopy compromises axial resolution, hindering accurate 3D structural analysis. This challenge is particularly pronounced in label-free imaging of thick, heterogeneous tissues, where assumptions about data distribution (e.g. sparsity, label-specific distribution, and lateral-axial similarity) and system priors (e.g. independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.

arxiv-2502-00510.title: Understanding and Optimizing Agentic Workflows via Shapley value
arxiv-2502-00510.creator: Yingxuan Yang, Bo Huang, Siyuan Qi, Chao Feng, Haoyi Hu, Yuxuan Zhu, Jinbo Hu, Haoran Zhao, Ziyi He, Xiao Liu, Muning Wen, Zongyu Wang, Lin Qiu, Xuezhi Cao, Xunliang Cai, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang
arxiv-2502-00510.description: Abstract Agentic workflows have become the dominant paradigm for building complex AI systems, orchestrating specialized components, such as planning, reasoning, action execution, and reflection, to tackle sophisticated real-world tasks. However, systematically analyzing and optimizing these workflows remains challenging due to intricate component interdependencies and the lack of principled attribution methods.

arxiv-2503-13119.title: OSLO-IC: On-the-Sphere Learned Omnidirectional Image Compression with Attention Modules and Spatial Context Thanks: The authors gratefully acknowledge that this work has been supported by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) under project number 418866191.
arxiv-2503-13119.creator: Paul Wawerek-López 1 , Navid Mahmoudian Bidgoli, Pascal Frossard 2 , André Kaup 1 , and Thomas Maugey 3
arxiv-2503-13119.description: Abstract Developing effective 360-degree (spherical) image compression techniques is crucial for technologies like virtual reality and automated driving. This paper advances the state-of-the-art in on-the-sphere learning (OSLO) for omnidirectional image compression framework by proposing spherical attention modules, residual blocks, and a spatial autoregressive context model. These improvements achieve a 23.1 % 23.

arxiv-2511-22060.title: Nonlinear Optical Quantum Communication with a Two-Dimensional Perovskite Light Source
arxiv-2511-22060.creator: Shuyue Feng, Zijian Gan, Camryn J. Gloor, Wei You, Andrew M. Moran
arxiv-2511-22060.description: Abstract Two–dimensional organic-–inorganic hybrid perovskite (2D-OIHP) quantum wells are emerging as promising light sources for quantum communication technologies, owing to their ability to generate polarization–encoded optical signals. In this work, we explore how nonlinear optical phenomena can be exploited for quantum information applications, demonstrating the versatility that arises from resonant coupling among excited states.

plos-pone-0003556.title: Neural Correlates of Hate
plos-pone-0003556.creator: Semir Zeki, John Paul Romaya
plos-pone-0003556.description: PLOS ONE research article. In this work, we address an important but unexplored topic, namely the neural correlates of hate. In a block-design fMRI study, we scanned 17 normal human subjects while they viewed the face of a person they hated and also faces of acquaintances for whom they had neutral feelings

pmc-10672895.title: Microcatheter-Directed Thrombolysis Using Recombinant Tissue Plasminogen Activator for the Treatment of Acute Superior Mesenteric Artery Embolism: A Case Report
pmc-10672895.creator: Yang-Won Kim, Ho-Cheol Choi, Won-Jeong Yang, Byeong-Ju Koo, Jae-Kyeong Ahn, Jeong-Pyo Lee, Jae-Bum Na, Sa-Hong Jo, Sung-Eun Park, Jung-Ho Won, Nicola Troisi
pmc-10672895.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) is a life-threatening condition, and in 50% of patients, AMI is caused by acute superior mesenteric artery (SMA) embolism. Endovascular treatment is increasingly being considered the primary modality in selected cases. Many studies have reported that percutaneous aspiration embolectomy using a guiding catheter and thrombolysis with recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) are effective in treating SMA embolism. However, no reports on treating SMA embolism using rtPA administered via a microcatheter exist.

pmc-10713981.title: Associate plant parasitic nematodes to weed species in some newly reclaimed lands
pmc-10713981.creator: Ghena Mamdouh AbdelRazek, Mohamed Abdelaziz Balah
pmc-10713981.description: Plant-parasitic nematodes (PPNs) are vital soil organisms well-known to damage and reduce crop yield worldwide. Surveys were attempts to determine the impact of weed species on the communities and composition of nematodes in barley, wheat, quinoa, eggplant, and tomato crops in Alexandria and Ismailia regions of Egypt.

pmc-10748185.title: A Novel Correction Methodology to Improve the Performance of a Low-Cost Hyperspectral Portable Snapshot Camera
pmc-10748185.creator: Andrea Genangeli, Giovanni Avola, Marco Bindi, Claudio Cantini, Francesco Cellini, Ezio Riggi, Beniamino Gioli
pmc-10748185.description: The development of spectral sensors (SSs) capable of retrieving spectral information have opened new opportunities to improve several environmental and agricultural practices, e.g., crop breeding, plant phenotyping, land use monitoring, and crop classification. The SSs are classified as multispectral and hyperspectral (HS) based on the number of the spectral bands resolved and sampled during data acquisition.

pmc-12363070.title: Level of job satisfaction and its associated factors among midwives working in public health institutions, Northwest Ethiopia: a multi-center study
pmc-12363070.creator: Nebiyu Solomon Tibebu, Berihun Agegn Mengistie, Saron Abeje Abiye, Paulos Abeje, Selamawit Tilahun, Sosina Belay, Geremew Azene, Belayneh Ayanaw Kassie
pmc-12363070.description: IntroductionMidwives are practitioners of midwifery and are recognized as indispensable professionals for lowering maternal mortality worldwide, particularly in low-income countries. Midwives who aren’t satisfied with their job challenge the prevention and control of maternal mortality and morbidity and had a surge in unfavorable patient outcomes.

pmc-12589443.title: Geometry optimization of broadband, planar, spiral inductors via continuous trace width modulation
pmc-12589443.creator: J Cañada, J M López-Villegas, N Vidal, S F Nagle, L F Velásquez-García
pmc-12589443.description: Variable-width planar inductors—commonly referred to as tapered inductors—have been shown to outperform their constant-width counterparts at specific target frequencies. This study extends that concept to the design of broadband inductors operating from DC to the low RF band (up to several hundred MHz), leveraging continuous trace width modulation to enhance performance.

pmc-12608236.title: Multivariate Frequency and Amplitude Estimation for Unevenly Sampled Data Using and Extending the Lomb–Scargle Method
pmc-12608236.creator: Martin Seilmayer, Thomas Wondrak, Ferran Garcia
pmc-12608236.description: The Lomb–Scargle method (LSM) constitutes a robust method for frequency and amplitude estimation in cases where data exhibit irregular or sparse sampling. Conventional spectral analysis techniques, such as the discrete Fourier transform (FT) and wavelet transform, rely on orthogonal mode decomposition and are inherently constrained when applied to non-equidistant or fragmented datasets, leading to significant estimation biases.

pmc-12750296.title: Job Loss and Early-onset Dementia Risk in Middle-aged Adults: A Longitudinal Study☆
pmc-12750296.creator: Heejoo Park, Jian Lee, Youngsun Park, Juho Sim, Byungyoon Yun, Jin-Ha Yoon
pmc-12750296.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEarly-onset dementia poses a significant public health challenge, particularly due to its profound impact on working-age individuals (under 65 years). This study investigated the association between job loss and early-onset dementia in middle-aged adults in Republic of Korea.MethodsUsing National Health Insurance Service data in the Republic of Korea, we analyzed participants aged 45–54 years who were employed by private companies and who underwent health checkups between 2009 and 2010.

pmc-13084558.title: Traumatic brain injury recovery prediction by harmonizing real brain CT and synthetic brain MRI: a pilot study
pmc-13084558.creator: Yiming Che, Amogh Manoj Joshi, Jay Shah, Md Mahfuzur Rahman Siddiquee, Catherine D Chong, Simona Nikolova, Gina Dumkrieger, Baoxin Li, Teresa Wu, Todd J Schwedt
pmc-13084558.description: To enhance the prediction of traumatic brain injury (mTBI) outcomes, we propose a deep learning approach that integrates brain computed tomography (CT) scans with corresponding synthetic T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (T1-MRI). Our method significantly outperforms the prediction using CT scans alone. TRACK-TBI Pilot dataset, which includes imaging and clinical outcome data from patients with TBI, is studied.

pmc-13250012.title: A critical review of chemical heterogeneity–driven microstructure control in steels
pmc-13250012.creator: Seung Hyun Lee, Ji Hoon Kim
pmc-13250012.description: This paper reviews a recent microstructure control strategy for steels based on intentional chemical heterogeneity, referred to as “chemically heterogeneous steels” or “chemically patterned steels.” This approach introduces controlled chemical inhomogeneity, which has traditionally been avoided, in order to diversify microstructural design and enhance mechanical properties.

pmc-13285133.title: A Large‐Area Broadband Multimodal Dual‐Resonant Haptic Device for Bidirectional Telerobotic and Augmented Interactions
pmc-13285133.creator: Jihun Son, Joon Hyeok Kang, Jaeha Park, Yoon‐Gi Ku, Yongjun Lee, Jinhyung Kim, Minjin Kim, Jun Hyeok Lee, Junsik Shin, Minwoo Song, Gui Won Hwang, Dongbum Pyo, Gwanghyun Jo, Jeong‐Hoi Koo, Young‐Min Kim, Changhyun Pang, Tae‐Heon Yang
pmc-13285133.description: Bidirectional haptic systems demand interfaces that combine sensing and actuation, enabling concurrent detection of tactile inputs and delivery of perceptually rich feedback across a broad frequency spectrum. However, most existing haptic technologies remain limited to simple tactile sensing or narrowband feedback, struggling to resolve continuous motions and simultaneous sensory cues required for naturalistic human‐machine interaction (HMI).
